texts.preamble: Ranjeet vs . Deepanshu & Ors. on 17 March, 2023 In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.1036/18 Fir No. 249/18 Ps : Nfc U/s 279/338 Ipc Cnr No. Dlse01 009338-2018 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu & Ors. Ranjeet Kumar S/o Sh. Kumarpal R/o Khaduiya, Post Khaduiya Distt. Kasganj, Uttar Pradesh. ....Claimant Versus 1. Deepanshu S/o Sh. Pappu Lal R/o H. No. Rzc -113-A Dabri Extension, New Delhi. .....driver/ respondent No. 1 3. Rajeev Kumar Pal S/o Sh. Chandra Pal R/o H. No. B-133A, Vikas Vihar East Vikas Nagar, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi. Mact No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 1/23 rpt 3. National Insurance Company. 2E/9, Jhandewalan Extension, New Delhi. ...Respondents Ranjeet vs . Deepanshu & Ors. on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84213507/ 1 Date of accident : 20.09.2018 Date of filing of Dar : 14.11.2018 Date of Decision : 17.03.2023 Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police official concerned and in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, same is treated as claim petition u/s 166 (1) r/w 166 (4) MV Act. 2. As per the investigation carried out by concerned police official on 20.09.2018, the information regarding present accident received through GD entry no. 27A. During investigation, it was found that an accident was occurred at Mathura Road near Bust Stop, Tribhuvan Complex where injured was standing and at 06.00 PM, an offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing no. DL 4SBX -5400, which was driven by R- 1 in a zig zag manner in high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit the injured injured/ Ranjeet due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injury. Injured returned to home in an auto and later on he was admitted in Trauma Center by his neighbor. Accordingly, the FIR in question recorded. MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 2/23 rpt Further as per the investigation carried out, a charge sheet was filed against R-1 for offence u/s u/s 279, 337, 338 IPC. Further present DAR is also filed. 3. In response to the DAR, R-1 & 2 appeared and contested th present case. Further, a joint reply / WS filed by R-1 & 2. In a nutshell, they denied the rash and negligent driving or the liability in the present case. It is furher claimed in the FIR itself claimant mentioned that he does not know the number of offending vehicle and some public person gave him the number of offending vehicle. It is further held that R-1 was holding valid DL of the offending vehicle in question which was insured with R-3. 4. In response to DAR reply filed by R-3/ insurance company. In nutshell in such reply, it is stated that no claim is payable by the R-3/ Ins. Co. as the driver / R-1 was not having an effective or valid DL at the time of accident. In fact, as per DL verification report, such DL was suspended during the period of 08.07.2018 to 07.10.2018 whereas the date of accident is 30.09.2018. Further, insurance company denied rash and negligent on the part of R-1 and instead claimed that accident took place due to negligence of injured himself. But insurance of the offending vehicle at the time of accident is not denied. 5. Following issues were framed on 14.12.2018 by my Ld. Predecessor: OPP 3. Relief. 6. Petitioner/injured stepped in the witness box as PW1 and tendered his examination in chief by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/5 including MLC, discharge summary, original medical documents, copy of Aadhar Card. 7. PW-1 was cross examined by counsel for R-1 & R-2 and same is adopted by R-3/ insurance company. 8. No other witness was examined on behalf of petitioner. 9. Fortunately, there is no permanent disability in the present case to the injured/ petitioner. 10. Further, as per record, although R-1/ driver and R-2/ owner both filed their examination in chief by way of affidavit, but only R-1/ driver examined himself as R1W1. Further such R-1W1 was cross examined by ld. Counsel for petitioner / claimant as well as by insurance company. 11. Further even the Insurance Company also examined on Sh. Raj Kumar Rana, its assistant as R3W1 and filed examination in chief by way of affidavit of such witness. Such R3W1 was not cross examined by R-1 & R-2. Further there was only one line cross examination of such witness by petitioner on the point since when he is working with R-3. 12. In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 15. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279,337, 338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. In National Ranjeet vs . Deepanshu & Ors. 16. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1, it is noted that he deposed on the line of original complaint on the basis of which FIR in question was registered regarding mode and manner in which accident took place. He further deposed that accident took place due to rash and negligent act of the R-1. 17. During his cross examination, PW-1/ injured admitted that MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 5/23 rpt he had not noted down the number of offending vehicle but someone had given him such number. He further admitted that he does not know name of the person who gave him the number of offending vehicle. He further admitted that he did not know the name of R-1 before the accident and even at present, he does not know his name. He further admitted that no person was available at the bus stop at the time of accident nor any vehicle was plying on the road. But he stated that 3-4 persons assembled after the accident and his neighbour took him to hospital. He further deposed that he do not even know the name of such neighbour as of now. He further admitted that he had no mobile phone at the time of accident. He further deposed that someone from the spot of accident informed the police about the accident. But he further deposed that he requested the person assembled there to take him to the hospital and even the driver of the offending vehicle to take him to hospital. He further denied the suggestion that he did not requested the driver to take him to hospital. He further denied the suggestion that he suddenly started crossing the road without taking any precaution. He further denied the suggestion that as such accident took place due to his own negligence as he was suddenly crossing the road. He further denied the suggestion that R-1 was not driving the offending vehicle in question or that R-1 did not cause the accident as alleged by injured. He further deposed that he saw the offending vehicle 20 steps and 2 minutes before the accident. 18. In his examination in chief by way of affidavit, R1/ driver / Deepanshu / R1W1 deposed that he did not cause the accident in question. Further, he repeated his stand as taken in his reply as already noted above. MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 6/23 rpt 19. During his cross examination by Ld counsel for petitioner, such R-1 / driver deposed that he is not arrested by the police officer regarding the accident in question and he denied the suggestion in this regard. As such, such witness was confronted with his arrest memo Ex.R1W1/P1 and he admitted his signature at point A on the same. He further admitted that he is facing criminal case trial in the concerned FIR in question. He further admitted that he has not made any verbal or written complaint against the concerned IO (regarding implicating him in the present case). 20. In the present case, a charge sheet is filed against the R-1 and same is pending trial before ld. Ilaka MM. on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84213507/ 4 question is not denied. Further, in reply to notice to u/s 133 MV Act, R-2 stated on 28.09.2018 that R1 was driving the motorcycle on the date of accident and he will produce along with motorcycle. Further, such, R-1 is arrested in the present case and no grievance is raised by R-1. Further there is a mechanical inspection report which is part of DAR, placed on record which also shows accidental impact on the vehicle. The issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner.
texts.arguments: Further the nature of injury caused to the injured also indicates that same is a road accident. Further there is medical documents of the injured prepared immediately after the accident. 21. As such, in view of the evidence proved on record, it is held that R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in question on the date of accident and due to his rash and negligent act, required to MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 7/23 rpt the standard of proof in a proceeding of present nature, injury is caused to the claimant / injured. CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE 22. But having held so, it is further argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company as well as by R-1 & 2 that in any case, it is a case of at least contributory negligence on the part of injured/ petitioner. It is further argued that he was a pedestrian and crossing the road which resulted into the accident in question. As such, 50% deduction be made on account of contributory negligence. 23. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that there is no question of contributory negligence on the part of injured. In fact, injured was standing near the bus stop and despite the place of accident near the bus stop, there was no zebra crossing and obviously after getting down from the bus, one has to cross the road. 24. In the preset case, it is not in dispute and no evidence to the contrary led that there is bus stop where the accident took place. Thus, such pedestrian has a right to cross the road at such bus stop and correspondingly it was a duty of R-1 to take care such passengers crossing the road. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 8/23 rpt Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 26. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 9/23 rpt (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 26.1. 26.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 26.7. 31. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. The rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case and taking all relevant factors including inflation, change of economy, policy being adopted by Reserve Bank of India from time to time, how long the case is pending, permanent injuries suffered by the victim, enormity of suffering, loss of future income, loss of enjoyment of life etc. into consideration. Interest MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 14/23 rpt is compensation for forbearance or detention of money and that interest being awarded to a party only for being kept out of the money which ought to have been paid to him. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 15/23 rpt Liability :- 34. In this case, defence of the insurance company taken in the reply as also deposed by its witness R3W1 Sh. Raj Kumar Rana is that R-1 was not having any effective and valid driving license at the time of accident on 20.09.2018. it is further, deposed by such witness that as per DL verification report, such license was already suspended during such period as noted above. As such, it is stated that there is thus a violation of policy and therefore, the insurance company may be given at least the recovery rights. It is further argued that there is no liability of insurance company under such circumstances at all. 35. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for R-1 & 2 that in this particular case, R-1 did enter into witness box. Further, he proved on record the legal remedy taken by him for illegal suspension of his license and same are pending before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. It is further argued that same are already proved on record as Ex.PW1/1 (colly, 52 pages). 36. In the background of such fact proved on record by insurance company as well as R-1, and having regard to the ratio and direction by Hon'ble Supreme Court, three judges bench judgment of "National Insurance Company v. Swaran Singh ((2004) 3SCC 297)", the compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company, but with liberty to recover the same from the R-1 & R-2 of the offending vehicle in question. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of literate MACT No.1036/18 Ranjeet Vs. Deepanshu No. 18/23 rpt persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
